statement: BC should approve new liquefied natural gas (LNG) export projects.

passages.title: Economic, budget promises the focus of week 2 of B.C. election campaign (Global News)
passages.quote: Interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson promised to double liquefied natural gas production by 2032 in the province, if elected, while NDP Leader David Eby announced  his government would double the export of critical minerals within five years. Doerkson said there’s a global energy crisis and “our allies in Asia and Europe desperately need Canadian LNG.” While Eby picked up on the same theme, saying B.C. has an abundance of critical minerals that other countries need. “Getting them to world markets means less dependence on the U.S., while creating family-supporting jobs and the prosperity needed to strengthen health care and public services,” said Eby, who was in Prince Rupert on Monday.

passages.title: Vancouver Sun: NDP, Conservatives both take credit for growing LNG sector
passages.quote: Liberal Premier Christy Clark, the liquefied natural gas industry has been slow to get going in the province but now has five terminals either under construction or awaiting final investment decisions. Article content Last year, the $40 billion LNG Canada Phase 1 began shipping gas to Asia. Article content Asked whether his government can take credit for the development of the sector, Eby’s answer was a definitive yes.

passages.title: Press release: BC Conservatives welcome LNG Canada Phase 2
passages.quote: The BC Energy Superpower Plan will : More than double natural gas production by 2032 and more than triple it by 2035; Designate the liquid-rich Montney Formation as a strategic provincial asset; Pass a 120 Day Permitting Act for major projects; Harmonize BC’s permitting, approvals and consultation with the federal government’s Bill C-39, so that BC-led projects are approved within one year; Invite foreign investors to Vancouver and make the case that British Columbia is the better place for their capital.

11.14 BC needs a common sense approach to power production centered around affordability, reliability, and
 independence. To achieve this, the Conservative Party of BC will:

passages.title: Hansard — May 25 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 183
passages.quote: So this minister and this Premier…. The Minister of Energy signs off on a letter from the Minister of Housing interfering in a council decision about banning natural gas. In what world does that make sense — that you have a Minister of Energy that thinks it’s okay for us to interfere in a council decision that bans natural gas? My question is to the Minister of Housing.
